The Danger of Changing Levels: Fallacies of Composition and Division Explained

Released Dec 16, 2025, 16 min

Play The Danger of Changing Levels: Fallacies of Composition and Division Explained on YouTube
Watch on YouTube

Two Fallacies for the Price of One: Composition and Division!

It's tempting to think that what's true of the parts must be true of the whole, and vice-versa. But that path is fraught with logical peril, often leading to comically terrible results!In this video, we break down the twin fallacies of composition and division, explore the logical structure of both good and bad arguments that 'change levels,' and show you the key question you MUST ask before making such a move.

By the end of this video, you will know:

  • What the Fallacy of Composition is (Part to Whole).
  • What the Fallacy of Division is (Whole to Part).
  • Why "The car weighs two tons, so the seat weighs two tons" is wrong.
  • Why "I own this shirt, so I own this button" is right.
  • The crucial test: Is the property preserved under composition/decomposition?

We also touch upon related concepts like Simpson's Paradox, Ecological Fallacies, and the Wisdom of Crowds.

Be skeptical when going from one level to another—always make your premises explicit!
